classification.text: 1. Heat oil in a large pot. Fry sliced onion until deep golden brown, then set aside.
2. In the same pot, add chopped garlic and saute for a minute. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
3. Return fried onion to pot. Add ginger paste and saute well.
4. Add cumin seeds, half the coriander seeds, and chopped green chillies. Stir quickly.
5. Add turmeric and red chilli powder. Saute for a couple of minutes.
6. Add chicken pieces, season with salt, and cook covered on medium-low for 15 minutes.
7. When oil separates from spices, add beaten yogurt on lowest heat. Sprinkle remaining coriander seeds and half the fenugreek leaves.
9. Sprinkle remaining kasuri methi and garam masala. Serve hot with naan.

1. Put mushrooms into a food processor with seasoning and pulse to a rough paste. Cook in a pan over high heat for about 10 mins, tossing frequently, to cook out the moisture. Spread on a plate to cool.
2. Heat a frying pan and add a little olive oil. Season the beef and sear for 30 secs on each side. Remove and leave to cool, then brush all over with mustard.

3. Lay cling film on a work surface and arrange Parma ham slices in slightly overlapping rows. Spread mushroom paste over the ham, then place beef in the middle. Roll tightly into a barrel shape. Chill for 15-20 mins.

4. Roll out puff pastry to a large rectangle. Remove cling film from beef and lay in the centre. Brush pastry with egg yolk, fold ends over, and wrap pastry around beef. Turn seam-side down on a baking sheet. Brush with egg and chill 15 mins.
5. Heat oven to 200C/400F/gas 6. Score pastry at 1cm intervals and glaze again with egg yolk.
6. Bake for 20 minutes, then lower to 180C/350F/gas 4 and cook for another 15 mins.
7. Rest for 10-15 mins before slicing and serving.
1. Heat the oil in a large pot. Add the onion and cook until translucent.
2. Drain the soaked chickpeas and add them to the pot together with the vegetable stock. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and cover. Simmer for 30 minutes.
3. In the meantime toast the cumin in a small ungreased frying pan, then grind them in a mortar. Add the garlic and salt and pound to a fine paste.
4. Add the paste and the harissa to the soup and simmer until the chickpeas are tender, about 30 minutes.
5. Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice and serve hot.
1. Preheat the oven to 160C/325F/Gas 3. Grease and line a 26cm/10in springform cake tin.
2. Mix all of the ingredients for the carrot cake, except the carrots and walnuts, together in a bowl until well combined. Stir in the carrots and walnuts.
3. Spoon the mixture into the cake tin and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the middle comes out clean.
4. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool for 10 minutes, then carefully remove from the tin and cool completely on a cooling rack.
5. For the icing, beat the cream cheese, caster sugar and butter together in a bowl until fluffy.
6. Spread the icing over the top of the cake with a palette knife.
1. Melt the butter with the oil in a large heavy-based pan. Add the onions and fry with the lid on for 10 mins until soft.
2. Sprinkle in the sugar and cook for 20 mins more, stirring frequently, until caramelised.
3. Add the garlic for the final few mins, then sprinkle in the flour and stir well.
4. Increase the heat and gradually add the wine, followed by the hot stock. Cover and simmer for 15-20 mins.
5. Turn on the grill and toast the bread. Ladle the soup into heatproof bowls.
6. Put a slice or two of toast on top and pile on the cheese. Grill until melted.

parsing.name: 6. Put a slice or two of toast on top and pile on the cheese. Grill until melted.
parsing.text: 6. Put a slice or two of toast on top and pile on the cheese. Grill until melted.

classification.text: 1. Heat the olive oil in a non-stick frying pan. Add the sliced onion and cook on medium heat for about 15 mins until completely softened. Crush in the garlic and cook for 2-3 mins further, then add the butter.
2. Once the butter is foaming, add the mushrooms and cook for around 5 mins until completely softened. Season everything well, then tip onto a plate.
3. Tip the flour into a bowl with a big pinch of salt and pepper, then toss the steak in the seasoned flour.
4. Add the steak pieces to the pan and fry for 3-4 mins, until well coloured. Tip the onions and mushrooms back in.
5. Whisk the creme fraiche, mustard and beef stock together, then pour into the pan. Cook over medium heat for around 5 mins.
6. Scatter with parsley, then serve with pappardelle or rice.

parsing.name: tip the flour
parsing.text: 3. Tip the flour into a bowl with a big pinch of salt and pepper, then toss the steak in the seasoned flour.

classification.text: 1. Cook the fusilli pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse under cold water.
2. In a large serving bowl, combine the cooled pasta with cherry tomatoes, cucumber, olives, feta cheese and red onion.
3. Whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar and dried oregano in a small bowl.
4. Pour the dressing over the pasta salad and toss to combine.
5. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve immediately or refrigerate for up to 24 hours.
1. Put the flour, eggs, milk, 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt into a bowl or large jug, then whisk to a smooth batter.
2. Set aside for 30 mins to rest if you have time, or start cooking straight away.
3. Set a medium frying pan over a medium heat and carefully wipe it with some oiled kitchen paper.
4. When hot, cook your pancakes for 1 min on each side until golden, keeping them warm in a low oven as you go.
5. Serve with lemon wedges and sugar, or your favourite filling.

parsing.name: put the flour eggs milk
parsing.text: 1. Put the flour, eggs, milk, 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt into a bowl or large jug, then whisk to a smooth batter.

classification.text: 1. Combine the sake, soy sauce, sesame oil and cornflour dissolved in water. Divide mixture in half.
2. Combine half the mixture with chicken pieces and toss to coat. Refrigerate for about 30 minutes.
3. In a medium frying pan, combine remaining sauce with chillies, vinegar and sugar. Mix together and add spring onion, garlic, water chestnuts and peanuts. Heat slowly until aromatic.
4. Remove chicken from marinade and saute until juices run clear.
5. When sauce is aromatic, add sauteed chicken and let simmer until sauce thickens.
1. Put the gammon in a very large pan with 2 litres water and bring to the boil. Drain off the water to remove saltiness. Recover with 2 litres cold water and bring to the boil again.
2. Put everything except the frozen peas into the pan and bring to the boil. Reduce to a simmer and cook for 1.5-2.5 hours, topping up water as needed.
3. When the ham is tender enough to shred, lift it out, peel off and discard the skin. Shred the meat while still hot.
4. Remove bay from the soup and stir in the frozen peas. Simmer for 1 min, then blend until smooth.
5. Mix the hot soup with most of the ham. Serve in bowls with remaining ham scattered on top, with crusty bread and butter.
Mix all the ingredients in the glaze together.
Heat up a skillet on medium-low heat.
Pan-fry the salmon on both sides until cooked through.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve immediately.
Add the ginger, garlic, soy sauce, sake and sugar to a bowl and whisk to combine. Add the chicken, then stir to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Add 1 inch of vegetable oil to a heavy bottomed pot and heat until the oil reaches 360 degrees F. Line a wire rack with 2 sheets of paper towels and get your tongs out. Put the potato starch in a bowl.
Add a handful of chicken to the potato starch and toss to coat each piece evenly.
Fry the karaage in batches until the exterior is a medium brown and the chicken is cooked through. Transfer the fried chicken to the paper towel lined rack.

Tip the beef stock along with 500ml of water into a large saucepan. Sit the onion and ginger in a frying pan over a high heat and char on all sides, around 3-5 mins. Once charred, add to the beef stock. In the same pan, toast the spices for 2-3 mins and once they begin to smell fragrant, add them to the beef stock as well. Bring the stock to the boil, then turn to a simmer and cook for 30 mins before straining.
Meanwhile, cut the fat from the steak and wrap in cling film, then put into the freezer for 15 mins. Slice it thinly, then cover with cling film again and pop into the fridge.

Taste the beef stock and use the palm sugar, fish sauce and soy to season. Cook the noodles according to package instructions and split between two bowls, topping each with the sliced beef. Bring the stock to the boil and then pour into the bowls. Top each with the spring onions, chilli slices and herbs. Serve with the lime wedges to squeeze over.
Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole dish and stir-fry the mushrooms until they start to soften. Add the chicken legs and cook briefly on each side to colour them a little.
Pour in the passata, crumble in the stock cube and stir in the olives. Season with black pepper.
Cover and simmer for 40 mins until the chicken is tender.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with pasta and a salad, or mash and green veg.
Preheat oven to 180C/350F/Gas 4 and line a baking tray with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, sugar and baking powder in a bowl and rub in the cubed butter until the mixture looks like breadcrumbs, then mix in the dried fruit.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg and milk together with the vanilla extract.
Add the egg mixture to the dry ingredients and stir with a spoon until the mixture just comes together as a thick, lumpy dough.
Place golfball-sized spoons of the mixture onto the prepared baking tray.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, until golden-brown. Remove from the oven, allow to cool for a couple of minutes then turn them out onto a wire rack to cool.
In a wok add chicken broth and wait for it to boil.
Next add salt, sugar, white pepper, sesame seed oil.
When the chicken broth is boiling add the vegetables to the wok.
To thicken the sauce, whisk together 1 tablespoon of cornstarch and 2 tablespoon of water in a bowl and slowly add to your soup until it's the right thickness.
Next add 1 egg slightly beaten with a knife or fork and add it to the soup slowly and stir for 8 seconds.
Serve the soup in a bowl and add the green onions on top.
Season the salmon fillets with salt and pepper. Pan-fry in a hot skillet with a little oil for 3-4 minutes on each side until cooked through. Allow to cool slightly, then flake into large chunks.
Arrange the mixed salad leaves on two plates. Top with avocado slices, cucumber and cherry tomatoes.
Scatter the flaked salmon over the salad.
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper and serve immediately.

Make 3 slashes on each of the drumsticks. Mix together the soy, honey, oil, tomato puree and mustard. Pour this mixture over the chicken and coat thoroughly. Leave to marinate for 30 mins at room temperature or overnight in the fridge. Heat oven to 200C/fan 180C/gas 6.
Tip the chicken into a shallow roasting tray and cook for 35 mins, turning occasionally, until the chicken is tender and glistening with the marinade.
Heat butter in a large skillet on medium heat. Add the onion and cook a few minutes, until translucent.
Mix in the chopped corned beef and potatoes. Spread out evenly over the pan. Increase the heat to high or medium high and press down on the mixture with a metal spatula.
Do not stir, but let them brown. Use a metal spatula to peek underneath and see if they are browning. If nicely browned, flip sections over so that they brown on the other side. Press down again.
Continue to cook until the potatoes and the corned beef are nicely browned.
Remove from heat, stir in chopped parsley. Add plenty of freshly ground black pepper, and salt to taste.
Heat a wok or large frying pan until smoking hot.
Pour in the oil and swirl around the pan, then tip in the beef strips and chilli.
Cook, stirring all the time, until the meat is lightly browned, about 3 mins.
Cook until heated through and the sauce coats the meat.
Stir in the basil leaves and serve with plain rice.
1. For the dough, place lard, warm water and salt in a large kneading bowl and stir. Add flour and oregano and knead for five minutes. Let rest covered for at least half an hour.

2. For the filling, blanch tomatoes, peel and cube. Saute garlic and onions until translucent. Brown the meat at high heat. Season with herbs, add tomatoes. Simmer for a few minutes. Mix in boiled cubed eggs.
3. Roll out dough, cut circles 12-15cm in diameter. Place filling in each, fold over and seal edges with a fork.
4. Brush empanadas with egg wash and bake for about 25 min or until golden.
1. Preheat the oven to 180C/Gas mark 4. Brown the chicken pieces in batches in butter and olive oil, seasoning with salt and pepper.
2. Fry the onions for 10 minutes until softened. Add the peppers and cook for another 5 minutes.
3. Add the chorizo, sun-dried tomatoes and garlic and cook for 2-3 minutes.
4. Add the rice, stirring to coat in oil. Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, bay leaves and thyme. Pour in the stock and wine.
5. Press the rice down, place the chicken on top. Add the lemon wedges and olives.
6. Cover and cook in the oven for 50 minutes until rice is cooked and chicken juices run clear.
1. Preheat the oven to 180C (350F). Grease a cake pan and line it with baking paper.
2. Break the four eggs with the sugar and beat until they have tripled in volume and become fluffy.
3. Sift the flour and fold into the egg mixture, preserving as much air as possible. Add the melted butter and mix until combined.
4. Add cinnamon, pinch of salt and vanilla extract.
5. Add the diced apple to the batter and gently fold them in so evenly distributed.
6. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan and smooth the top.
7. Place apple slices on top and press lightly. Sprinkle with almond shavings if desired.
8. Bake for about 45-50 minutes, or until a wooden skewer comes out clean.
9. Cool in the mold, then remove and cool completely. Sprinkle with powdered sugar.

parsing.name: add cinnamon
parsing.text: 4. Add cinnamon, pinch of salt and vanilla extract.

classification.text: 1. Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Toss the pumpkin in a roasting tin with half the oil and seasoning, then roast for 30 mins until golden and tender.

2. Put the remaining oil in a pan with the onion, ginger and lemongrass. Gently cook for 8-10 mins until softened. Stir in the curry paste for 1 min, followed by the roasted pumpkin, most of the coconut milk and the stock.
3. Bring to a simmer, cook for 5 mins, then fish out the lemongrass. Cool for a few mins, then blend until smooth.
4. Return to the pan to heat through, seasoning with salt, pepper, lime juice and sugar.
5. Serve drizzled with the remaining coconut milk and scattered with chilli.
1. Preheat fryer to 350F. Thoroughly mix together all the spice mix ingredients.
2. Combine spice mix with flour, brown sugar and salt.

3. Dip chicken pieces in egg white to lightly coat them, then transfer to flour mixture. Turn a few times and make sure the flour mix is really stuck to the chicken. Repeat with all the chicken pieces.
4. Let chicken pieces rest for 5 minutes so crust has a chance to dry a bit.
5. Fry chicken in batches. Breasts and wings should take 12-14 minutes, and legs and thighs will need a few more minutes. Chicken is done when thermometer reads 165F.
6. Let chicken drain on paper towels when it comes out of the fryer. Serve hot.
1. Chop the spice paste ingredients and blend in a food processor until fine.
2. Heat the oil in a stew pot, add the spice paste, cinnamon, cloves, star anise, and cardamom and stir-fry until aromatic.
3. Add the beef and pounded lemongrass and stir for 1 minute. Add the coconut milk, tamarind juice, water, and simmer on medium heat, stirring frequently until the meat is almost cooked.
4. Add the kaffir lime leaves, toasted coconut, sugar, stirring to blend well with the meat.
5. Lower the heat to low, cover and simmer for 1 to 1.5 hours or until the meat is really tender and the gravy has dried up.
6. Add more salt and sugar to taste. Serve immediately with steamed rice.

1. For the pastry: dice butter and freeze until hard. Pulse flour with half the butter to breadcrumb texture. Add lemon juice and 100ml iced water, pulse to a dough. Pulse in remaining butter just a few times.
2. Roll out to a rectangle, fold ends into middle, then fold in half. Repeat 3 more times with 15 min rests between each. Chill 30 mins.
3. For the filling: melt butter and stir in all other filling ingredients.
4. Roll pastry slightly thicker than a coin, cut 8 rounds about 12cm across. Place filling in each, seal edges, flip smooth-side up, and flatten with rolling pin until fruit just pokes through.
5. Cut 2 slits in each cake, brush with egg white and sprinkle with sugar.
6. Bake for 15-20 mins until golden brown and sticky. Cool on a rack.
1. Season the salmon fillets and pan-fry in a skillet over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side. Set aside.

2. For hollandaise, whisk egg yolks with lemon juice in a heatproof bowl set over simmering water. Slowly drizzle in the melted butter while whisking constantly until thick and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
3. Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer with white vinegar. Crack each egg into a small bowl and gently slide into the water. Poach for 3-4 minutes.
4. Place toasted muffin halves on plates. Top each with a salmon fillet, then a poached egg.
5. Spoon hollandaise over the top. Garnish with fresh dill and serve immediately.
1. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion for 1-2 mins just until softened.
2. Add the chicken and fry for 7-10 mins until cooked through and the onions have turned golden.
3. Grate over the ginger, stir through the harissa to coat everything and cook for 1 min more.
4. Tip in the apricots, chickpeas and couscous, then pour over the stock and stir once.
5. Cover with a lid or foil and leave for about 5 mins until the couscous has soaked up all the stock and is soft.
6. Fluff up the couscous with a fork and scatter over the coriander to serve.
Bake: 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours 5 minutes
Oven: Start at 180C / 160C fan / Gas 4, reduce to 160C / 140C fan / Gas 3
1. Put almonds in a small bowl and pour over boiling water to cover. Leave for 5 mins then drain and dry.
2. Preheat oven to 180C/160C fan/Gas 4. Line a deep 20cm cake tin with baking parchment.
3. Beat butter until soft. Add sugar and beat until light and fluffy. Stir in orange zest and apricot jam.
4. Sieve flour and baking powder together. Add eggs to creamed butter and sugar a little at a time, beating well between each addition.
5. Add remaining flour and ground almonds and mix well. Mix in milk, then add dried fruit and cherries.
6. Spoon into prepared tin and spread level. Arrange whole almonds in neat circles on top.
7. Bake for 45 mins. Lower oven to 160C/140C fan/Gas 3 and cook for a further 60-80 minutes.
8. Heat milk and sugar until dissolved, brush over hot cake, return to oven for 2-3 mins.
9. Cool in tin. When cold, wrap in foil and keep for at least 2 days before cutting.
So my mom used to make this all the time when I was growing up and I finally got the recipe from her last Christmas. It's one of those dishes that takes forever but is SO worth it.

You'll need about 3 tsp goose fat (or butter works too), 600g beef shin cut into chunks, 100g bacon lardons, 350g shallots, 250g chestnut mushrooms, 2 sliced garlic cloves, 1 bouquet garni, 1 tbs tomato puree, 750ml red wine (use a decent one!), 600g celeriac for the mash, 2 tbs olive oil, sprigs of fresh thyme and rosemary, 2 bay leaves, and 4 cardamom pods.
Heat a large casserole pan and add the goose fat. Season the beef and fry until golden brown, about 3-5 mins, then turn over and fry the other side. Do this in 2-3 batches.
In the same pan, fry the bacon, shallots, mushrooms, garlic and bouquet garni until lightly browned.
Mix in the tomato puree and cook for a few mins.
Return the beef and any juices to the pan.
Pour over the wine and about 100ml water. Bring to the boil and scrape the bottom of the pan.
Heat oven to 150C/fan 130C/gas 2. Cover and cook for 3 hrs.
For the celeriac mash, peel and cube the celeriac, fry in olive oil for 5 mins.
Add herbs and 200ml water, simmer 25-30 mins. Crush with a potato masher and finish with olive oil.

For the sauce: 3/4 cup water, 1/2 cup chicken stock, 1/4 cup duck sauce, 3 tbs soy sauce, 2 tbs honey, 1 tbs rice vinegar, 2 tbs sesame seed oil, 1/2 tbs gochujang, 2 tbs starch, 1 clove garlic, 2 chopped spring onions, 1 tsp ginger

In a bowl, add 2 Cups of water, 2 Tablespoon soy sauce, 2 Tablespoon white vinegar, sherry cooking wine, 1/4 Teaspoon white pepper, minced ginger, minced garlic, hot pepper, ketchup, hoisin sauce, and sugar. Mix together well and set aside.
In a bowl, add the chicken, 1 pinch of salt, 1 pinch of white pepper, 2 egg whites, and 3 Tablespoon of corn starch
Deep fry the chicken at 350 degrees for 3-4 minutes or until it is golden brown
Add the sauce to the wok and then the broccoli and wait until it is boiling. Thicken with cornstarch slurry. Add in the chicken and stir-fry for a minute and serve

parsing.name: In a bowl, add the chicken, 1 pinch of salt, 1 pinch of white pepper, 2 egg whites, and 3 Tablespoon of corn starch
parsing.text: In a bowl, add the chicken, 1 pinch of salt, 1 pinch of white pepper, 2 egg whites, and 3 Tablespoon of corn starch

classification.text: ok so you need 1/2 lb beef, pinch salt, pinch pepper, 2 tsp sesame seed oil, 1/2 egg, 3 tbs starch, 5 tbs oil, 1/4 lb noodles, 1/2 cup onion, 1 tsp minced garlic, 1 tsp ginger, 1 cup bean sprouts, 1 cup mushrooms, 1 cup water, 1 tbs oyster sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp soy sauce
In a bowl, add the beef, salt, 1 pinch white pepper, 1 Teaspoon sesame seed oil, 1/2 egg, corn starch,1 Tablespoon of oil and mix together.
In a 6 qt pot add your noodles to boiling water until the noodles are submerged and boil on high heat for 10 seconds. After your noodles is done boiling strain and cool with cold water.
Add 2 Tablespoons of oil, beef and cook on high heat untill beef is medium cooked.
In a wok add 2 Tablespoon of oil, onions, minced garlic, minced ginger, bean sprouts, mushrooms, peapods and 1.5 cups of water
To make the sauce, add oyster sauce, 1 pinch white pepper, 1 teaspoon sesame seed oil, sugar, and 1 Teaspoon of soy sauce.
Next add the beef to wok and stir-fry
This is a classic one-pot recipe thats been in my family for generations. The trick is to cook it low and slow so the lamb just falls apart.
You need about 2 lbs lamb shoulder (or mutton if you can find it), cut into chunks
handful of chopped parsley for serving

Melt butter in a heavy dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb in batches - don't crowd the pan or it'll steam instead of brown. Remove and set aside. Add the onions and cook until softened about 5 minutes. Add the carrots and cook another couple minutes. Return the lamb to the pot with any juices. Pour in the stock add the tomato paste Worcestershire thyme and bay leaves. Bring to a boil then add the potatoes pressing them down into the liquid. Cover tightly and simmer on low heat for about 2 hours checking occasionally. The stew is done when the lamb is falling apart tender. Season with salt and pepper scatter with parsley and serve with crusty soda bread.

parsing.name: you need
parsing.text: You need about 2 lbs lamb shoulder (or mutton if you can find it), cut into chunks

classification.text: Heat oven to 200C/fan 180C/gas 6. Boil the potatoes for 15-20 mins until tender. Drain, return to the pan, then mash with some seasoning and 2 tsp of the paprika.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large pan, then fry the onions and garlic for a few mins until softened. Stir in the remaining paprika for 1 min, add the tomatoes, then, bring to a simmer. Tip into a large ovenproof dish, then stir in the chicken, peppers, olives and some seasoning.
Spoon over the mash, then bake for 15 mins until the mash is golden on top and the sauce is bubbling.

In a wok add chicken broth and wait for it to boil. Next add salt, sugar, sesame seed oil, white pepper, hot pepper sauce, vinegar and soy sauce and stir for few seconds. Add Tofu, mushrooms, black wood ear mushrooms to the wok. To thicken the sauce, whisk together 1 Tablespoon of cornstarch and 2 Tablespoon of water in a bowl and slowly add to your soup until it's the right thickness. Next add 1 egg slightly beaten with a knife or fork and add it to the soup and stir for 8 seconds. Serve the soup in a bowl and add the bbq pork and sliced green onions on top.
So the key to good fried rice is using DAY OLD rice. Seriously, don't skip this step or it'll be gummy and gross. I learned this the hard way lol

1 lb chicken thighs (boneless), 1 tsp salt, 3 tablespoons canola oil, 3 large eggs, 2/3 cup diced onion, 2 cloves minced garlic, 2 tsp ground ginger, 1 large carrot diced, 2/3 cup peas, 4 cups cooked jasmine rice (day old!), 2 sliced scallions, 1/2 tsp Chinese five spice powder, 2.5 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame seed oil

First chop the chicken into small cubes and sprinkle with salt. Set aside 10 min. Then scramble the eggs in 1 tbsp oil, break into small pieces, set aside. Cook the chicken in another tbsp of oil for 4-5 minutes. Set aside. Clean the wok. Add last tbsp of oil, cook onions 1 minute, add garlic and ginger, cook 30 seconds. Add carrots, cook 2 minutes. Add peas.

Now here's where it gets good - add the rice on top of the vegetables and smash any clumps. Add scallion whites and five spice. Drizzle soy sauce and sesame oil over everything and stir. Add back the chicken and eggs and the dark green scallion parts. Cook 1-2 more minutes and serve!

parsing.name: chicken thighs (boneless), 1 tsp salt, 3 tablespoons canola oil, 3 large eggs, 2/3 cup diced onion, 2 cloves minced garlic, 2 tsp ground ginger, 1 large carrot diced, 2/3 cup peas, 4 cups cooked jasmine rice (day old!), 2 sliced scallions, 1/2 tsp Chinese five spice powder, 2.5 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame seed oil
parsing.text: 1 lb chicken thighs (boneless), 1 tsp salt, 3 tablespoons canola oil, 3 large eggs, 2/3 cup diced onion, 2 cloves minced garlic, 2 tsp ground ginger, 1 large carrot diced, 2/3 cup peas, 4 cups cooked jasmine rice (day old!), 2 sliced scallions, 1/2 tsp Chinese five spice powder, 2.5 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame seed oil

classification.text: Put the oil, onions, celery, carrots, potatoes and bay leaves in a big casserole dish, or two saucepans. Fry gently until the onions are softened – about 10-15 mins. Fill the kettle and boil it. Stir in the tomato purée, sugar, vinegar, chopped tomatoes and passata, then crumble in the stock cubes. Add 1 litre boiling water and bring to a simmer. Cover and simmer for 15 mins until the potato is tender, then remove the bay leaves. Purée with a stick blender until very smooth. Season to taste and add a pinch more sugar if it needs it.
To serve, reheat the soup, stirring in the milk – try not to let it boil. Serve in small bowls.

You need: 1/2 lb beef, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp sesame seed oil, 1 pinch pepper, 1 egg white, 3 tbs starch, 4 tbs oil, 1 tsp ginger, 1 tsp garlic, 3/4 cup onion, 1/2 cup carrots, 3/4 cup green pepper, 1 cup celery, 1 cup mushrooms, 1 tbs cooking wine, 1 cup water, 1 tbs oyster sauce, 1/2 tsp hot sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tbs soy sauce
In a bowl, add the beef, salt, sesame seed oil, white pepper, egg white, 2 Tablespoon of corn starch and 1 Tablespoon of oil.
First Cook the beef by adding 2 Tablespoon of oil until the beef is golden brown. Set aside
In a wok add 1 Tablespoon of oil, minced ginger, minced garlic and stir-fry for few seconds. Next add all of the vegetables and then add sherry cooking wine and 1 cup of water.
To make the sauce add oyster sauce, hot pepper sauce, and sugar. add the cooked beef and 1 spoon of soy sauce
To thicken the sauce, whisk together 1 Tablespoon of cornstarch and 2 Tablespoon of water in a bowl and slowly add to your stir-fry until it's the right thickness.

parsing.name: first cook
parsing.text: First Cook the beef by adding 2 Tablespoon of oil until the beef is golden brown. Set aside

classification.text: I've been making this recipe for years and it's always a crowd pleaser. Way better than takeout and honestly pretty quick once you get the hang of it!

1 lb chicken thighs cut into 1-inch pieces, 1 large egg white, 1 tsp kosher salt, 2 tsp cornstarch. For the sauce you need 1/4 cup pineapple juice, 1/4 cup white vinegar, 1/4 cup ketchup, 3 tablespoons brown sugar. Also need 10 oz pineapple chunks, 4 tsp cooking oil, 1 chopped red pepper, 1 chopped yellow pepper, 1 tsp minced ginger
Coat chicken with egg white, salt and cornstarch. Let sit 15 minutes.
Make the sauce by whisking pineapple juice vinegar ketchup salt and brown sugar together.
Heat pan SUPER hot - this is key. Add 1 tbsp oil, spread chicken in one layer, don't touch it for 1 minute. Flip and fry other side 1 minute. Remove chicken.

Turn heat to medium, add remaining oil. Fry peppers and ginger 1 minute. Add pineapple chunks and sauce. Turn heat back to high. When simmering add chicken back. Simmer 1-2 minutes until chicken is done. Serve over rice.

parsing.name: chicken thighs cut into 1-inch pieces, 1 large egg white, 1 tsp kosher salt, 2 tsp cornstarch. For the sauce you need 1/4 cup pineapple juice, 1/4 cup white vinegar, 1/4 cup ketchup, 3 tablespoons brown sugar. Also need 10 oz pineapple chunks, 4 tsp cooking oil, 1 chopped red pepper, 1 chopped yellow pepper, 1 tsp minced ginger
parsing.text: 1 lb chicken thighs cut into 1-inch pieces, 1 large egg white, 1 tsp kosher salt, 2 tsp cornstarch. For the sauce you need 1/4 cup pineapple juice, 1/4 cup white vinegar, 1/4 cup ketchup, 3 tablespoons brown sugar. Also need 10 oz pineapple chunks, 4 tsp cooking oil, 1 chopped red pepper, 1 chopped yellow pepper, 1 tsp minced ginger

classification.text: 1. Mix the lemon juice with the paprika and red onions in a large shallow dish. Slash each chicken thigh three times, then turn them in the juice and set aside for 10 mins.
2. Mix all of the marinade ingredients together and pour over the chicken. Give everything a good mix, then cover and chill for at least 1 hr.
3. Heat the grill. Lift the chicken pieces onto a rack over a baking tray. Brush over a little oil and grill for 8 mins on each side or until lightly charred and completely cooked through.
1. In a bowl, add chicken, salt, white pepper, ginger juice and mix well. Set aside.
2. Rinse the rice a couple of times and drain.
3. Add 2 litres of water to a large pot and bring to the boil on high heat. Once the rice porridge starts to boil, reduce to low heat and stir once every 8-10 minutes for 20-25 minutes.
4. After 25 minutes, add a little more water if needed to adjust thickness.
5. Add the marinated chicken and leave on low heat for another 10 minutes.
6. Add spring onions, sliced ginger, a pinch of salt and white pepper. Stir for 10 seconds.
7. Serve in bowls. Garnish with fresh coriander.
1. Combine beef, crushed peppercorn, soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaves, lemon, and tomato sauce. Mix well. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
2. Put the marinated beef in a cooking pot with remaining marinade. Add water. Bring to the boil.
3. Add beef stock cube. Stir. Cover and cook for 40 minutes on low heat.
4. Turn the beef over. Add tomato paste. Continue cooking until beef is tender. Set aside.
5. Heat oil in a pan. Fry the potato until browned on both sides. Do the same with the carrots.
6. In 3 tablespoons of the cooking oil, saute onion and garlic until softened.
7. Pour in the sauce from the beef stew. Bring to the boil. Add the beef. Cook for 2 minutes.
8. Add butter and let it melt. Continue cooking until the sauce reduces by half.

classification.text: 1. Heat oven to 160C/140C fan/gas 3. Grease a deep 22cm square cake tin and line with baking parchment.
2. Beat the egg and milk together with a fork.
3. Gently melt the syrup, treacle, sugar and butter together in a large pan until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat.
4. Mix together the oatmeal, flour and ginger and stir into the syrup mixture, followed by the egg and milk.
5. Pour the mixture into the tin and bake for 50 mins to 1 hr until the cake feels firm and a little crusty on top.
6. Cool in the tin then wrap in parchment and foil. Keep for 3-5 days before eating -- it becomes softer and stickier the longer you leave it.
2. Heat the oil in a deep frying pan and fry the beef mince for 4-5 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon as it browns.
3. Add the onion and cook for 2-3 minutes, then stir in the tomato puree and cook for 2-3 more minutes.
4. Stir in the flour and cook for a further minute, then add the chopped mushrooms, the stout or beef stock and a couple of dashes of Worcestershire sauce.
5. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Set aside and leave to cool, then turn into a one litre pie dish.
6. Roll out the pastry to slightly larger than the pie dish. Drape over the dish, pressing firmly onto edges. Trim and flute the edges.
7. Cut leaf shapes from trimmings for decoration. Make slits for steam. Brush with beaten egg yolk.
8. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden-brown. Slice into wedges to serve.

1. Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Roast the peanuts on a baking tray for 5 mins until golden brown. Roughly chop when cool. Reduce oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4.
2. Heat 2 tbsp coconut cream in a large casserole dish with a lid. Add the curry paste and fry for 1 min, then stir in the beef and fry until well coated and sealed.
3. Stir in the rest of the coconut with half a tin of water, the potatoes, onion, lime leaves, cinnamon, tamarind, sugar, fish sauce and most of the peanuts.
4. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 2 hrs in the oven until the beef is tender.
5. Sprinkle with sliced chilli and the remaining peanuts, then serve straight from the dish with jasmine rice.

classification.text: 1. Pre-heat the oven to 180C/350F/Gas 4. Grease an 18cm round cake tin, line the base with greaseproof paper and grease the paper.
2. Cream the butter and sugar together in a bowl until pale and fluffy.
3. Beat in the eggs, one at a time, beating the mixture well between each one and adding a tablespoon of the flour with the last egg to prevent curdling.
4. Sift the flour and gently fold in, with enough milk to give a mixture that falls slowly from the spoon. Fold in the lemon zest.
5. Spoon the mixture into the prepared tin and lightly level the top.
6. Bake on the middle shelf for 30-40 minutes, or until golden-brown on top and a skewer comes out clean.
7. Remove and set aside to cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack and leave to cool completely.

classification.text: 1. Heat the oil in your largest pan, add the onion and fry for 3 mins to soften. Add the chicken and garlic, and cook until the chicken changes colour.
2. Add the curry paste, coconut milk, stock, lime leaves and fish sauce, then simmer for 12 mins.
3. Add the chopped onion tops, green beans and bamboo shoots and cook for 4-6 mins, until the beans are just tender.
4. Put the lime juice and basil in a narrow jug and blitz with a hand blender to make a smooth green paste.
5. Pour into the soup with the sliced spring onion and heat through.
6. Serve with lime wedges for a light lunch or supper.
Prep Time: Overnight soaking plus 20 minutes
1. Wash and soak the kidney beans overnight in plenty of water. Drain.

2. Place everything except the flour, potato and coconut milk in a large pot. Cover with water and bring to the boil. Skim off any scum at the top. Reduce to a gentle boil and cook for 1 hr 15 mins until beans are tender and falling apart.
3. Add the potato and coconut milk and continue cooking for 15 minutes.
4. Make basic dough for spinner dumplings: mix the flour and water with a pinch of salt until you have a smooth dough. Rest for 5 minutes, then pinch off tablespoons and roll into cigarette shapes.
5. Add dumplings to the pot, stir well and continue cooking for another 15 minutes on a rolling boil.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning. The salt from the pigtails should season the dish sufficiently.

1. In a medium pot, heat the olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until they start to caramelise. Add the carrots and cook until they start to soften, about 4 more minutes.
2. Add the stock, water, potatoes, bay leaves, and black peppercorns. Season with salt and bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover and cook for 10 minutes.
3. Add the millet and cook for 15 more minutes until millet and potatoes are cooked.
4. Gently add the fish cubes. Stir and bring the soup to a simmer. The fish will cook through very fast, so make sure not to overcook. They are done when the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
5. Garnish with chopped fresh dill or parsley before serving.
